definition: To express an idea clearly and effectively; or, fluent and clear in speech.
exampleSentences: She articulated her argument so clearly that everyone understood.
An articulate speaker can inspire a whole audience.

definition: An educated guess or proposed explanation that can be tested.
exampleSentences: The scientist's hypothesis was that plants grow faster with music.
Before the experiment, we wrote down our hypothesis.
tip: A HYPO-THESIS is like a THESIS (idea) you put UNDER a microscope to test!

definition: Never done or known before; without previous example.
exampleSentences: The team achieved an unprecedented victory, winning every single game.
The discovery was unprecedented in the history of science.
tip: UN-PRECEDENT-ed — no PRECEDENT (example) exists before it!

definition: To combine different ideas or things to form a new whole.
exampleSentences: Good writers synthesize information from multiple sources.
The report synthesized data from three different studies.
tip: SYNTH-esize — like a music synthesizer combines sounds into something new!

definition: To publicly support or recommend a cause or policy; a person who does this.
exampleSentences: She advocates for equal access to education for all children.
The advocate spoke passionately about protecting the environment.
tip: An ADVOCATE uses their VOICE (voc) to speak up for others!

definition: Continued effort and determination despite difficulties or delay in achieving success.
exampleSentences: Through perseverance, she finally mastered the difficult piano piece.
The story of the inventor teaches us about the power of perseverance.
tip: PERSEVER-ance — you SEVERE (cut through) every obstacle!

definition: A particular way of thinking about something; a point of view.
exampleSentences: Reading books from different cultures gives us new perspectives.
From my perspective, teamwork is more important than individual talent.
tip: Your PERSPECTIVE is the lens through which you PER-SPECT (look through)!

definition: To accept or recognize that something is true or exists.
exampleSentences: It is important to acknowledge your mistakes and learn from them.
The author acknowledged the contributions of her research team.
tip: When you ACKNOWLEDGE, you give a KNOWLEDGE-able nod to the truth!
